claim: Mode-selective additive-noise stability of the N81 postselection obstruction
theorem: For the N81 rational centered pure-Gaussian family with m=Theta(R), uniform pure loss eta=1/R, h=O(R), and post-loss herald lower bound p>=w>=2^(-s), s=O(R^2 log R), apply rational Gaussian displacement noise after the known passive network and before loss: nu_H=2^(-[2s+ceil(log2(20000m))]) on herald modes and nu_S=R^(-a), a fixed positive constant, on all unheralded detector modes including retained outputs. The resulting input is full rank; its conditional output law is o(1)-close to the ideal N81 law for each fixed a>0.
proof: The H-noise global trace bound is delta_H<=sqrt(2m nu_H)<=w/100. With p>=w, conditioning gives TV<=delta_H/(p-delta_H)<=1/99. The S-noise channel is local to the unmeasured output subsystem, preserves the herald mass, commutes through uniform loss with variance scaled by eta, and satisfies T(rho,A_tau(rho))<=sqrt(tau(2E+m_S)). Since eta=1/R, conditional post-loss energy E<=eta(h+0.01), and m_S=O(R), S-noise contributes at most sqrt(nu_S O(1)).
cost: nu_H requires O(R^2 log R) denominator bits; nu_S=R^(-a) has O(log R) bits. Added numerical energy is O(m nu_S)<=O(R). Numerical m,h,1/eta, energy, input bits, epsilon^-1, and s=log2(1/w) are polynomial in R. The bound charges no inverse physical success probability.
baseline: Generic all-state trace-distance continuity certifies a fixed conditional error only for globally isotropic nu<=gamma^2 w^2/[2m(1+gamma)^2], exponentially small in R^2 log R. The mode-selective construction improves robustness only on the unheralded subsystem.
falsifier: An error in the N81 post-loss mass bound, the Weyl displacement-channel inequality, or the output-partition locality would invalidate the extension. If noise is applied before a mixing network without pulling back the covariance correctly, the herald can change.
sources: Optical postselection prior: Knill-Laflamme-Milburn, Nature 409 (2001), https://doi.org/10.1038/35051009
open_gate: Independent replay of the N81 rational optical compiler, source rounding, false-herald filter, and post-loss probability bound. Uniform inverse-polynomial noise on all modes erases this compiled conditional statistic by PC-03/PC-14, so the class-collapse implication applies only to the stated mode-selective family.
scope: Mathematical bounds are internally derived. The family-specific class implication is separately recorded as conditional in PC-02. No PP != BPP separation or runtime lower bound follows.

claim: A polynomial-bit sampler for the mode-selectively perturbed family would imply PP=BPP
theorem: Assuming the N81/N82 source/compiler candidate and its encoded-bit conditional gap, any uniform classical sampler with constant conditional-TV error for the full-rank mixed family in PC-01 and runtime polynomial in finite description length, numerical m,h,E,1/eta, epsilon^-1, and log(1/w) yields PP subseteq BPP, hence PP=BPP. The corresponding quantum sampling implication is PP=BQP.
proof: The H perturbation costs at most 1/99 conditionally; for fixed a>0, S perturbation tends to zero; a 0.01 sampler error and inherited compiler/filter error below 0.02 leave the N81 constant decision gap positive. A constant number of conditional samples and majority amplification decides each PP language.
cost: The numeric herald count and inverse loss are O(R); log inverse herald lower bound is s=O(R^2 log R); all rational perturbation descriptions have polynomial bit length. There is no physical rejection step.
baseline: Physical unconditional rejection costs expected 1/p and is not the abstract conditional sampling interface. The implication only excludes runtimes polynomial in log(1/p), not runtimes polynomial in 1/p.
falsifier: Independent replay that disproves the N81 optical compilation, post-loss lower bound, or final conditional gap blocks this consequence. The claim does not assert a separation.
sources: N81-N83 source/status cards and proof page work/astra_prior/web/pages/d-f3b89d44c7a3e836.html
open_gate: Independent proof audit and compiler replay for N81-N83.
scope: Conditional consequence; source-reported inherited reduction, not external validation.

claim: Uniform inverse-polynomial all-mode noise erases the N81 compiled conditional statistic
theorem: For the N81 centered pure-Gaussian family with rational detector-plane B, ||B||<=g=2^(-ell), ell>=R, d=Theta(R), binary herald h,h0=O(R), uniform loss eta=1/R, and any fixed integer a>=1, add isotropic displacement noise nu=R^(-a) to all detector modes before loss. The complete retained two-mode count law conditioned on the herald is TV-o(1) from vacuum, erasing the encoded constant-TV amplification; subleading probabilities may still encode information. The actual herald mass is p_ref(1+o(1)), p_ref=t^h/(1+t)^(2h+h0), t=eta nu, with log(1/p_ref)=O(R log R).
evidence: After all-mode additive noise the state has a positive Gaussian P representation because nu>g/(1-g). Its post-loss latent quadrature covariance is t(I+E), ||E||<=delta=g/((1-g)nu). Under the B=0 reference posterior conditioned on the binary herald, the standardized squared radius S has an explicit gamma moment-generating function. The Gaussian prior likelihood ratio r obeys |log r|<=C delta(2d+S), giving conditional latent chi-square <=exp(Cd delta)-1 and output TV O(sqrt(d delta)) by data processing. Since d delta=O(R^(a+1)2^(-R))->0, and the reference retained thermal modes have mean t->0, the retained law tends to vacuum. Full derivation: outputs/research/photonic_complexity/all_mode_noise_n81_proof.txt.
cost: d,h,h0,1/eta=O(R); nu=R^(-a) has O(log R) bits for fixed integer a; added input energy is d nu=O(R^(1-a)); the herald log inverse is O(R log R). The conditional comparison has no 1/p_ref loss.
baseline: The direct pure-source trace distance is at most g*sqrt(d/[2(1-g^2)]), and dividing it by p_ref is not sufficient when h is linear in R. The posterior positive-P comparison avoids this failure. This erases the N81 constant-TV encoded amplification on the supplied family; subleading probabilities may still encode information. It is not a sampler for arbitrary noisy Gaussian inputs.
falsifier: A covariance-convention error, failure of the positive-P threshold, incorrect herald-conditioned gamma law, or a failure of the likelihood-ratio chi-square bound would invalidate the candidate. Noise must be isotropic in the detector-mode basis before uniform loss.
open_gate: Independent review of the posterior covariance proof and replay of the inherited N81/N82 optical compiler; do not infer hardness/easiness for other noisy instances.
scope: Family-specific conditional-law erasure, not PP != BPP, a general noisy sampler, or a no-noise hardness refutation.

theorem: For a supplied finite-bit physical Gaussian density kernel with real entrywise nonnegative K and ell in a supplied number-preserving phase gauge and the required physical structure, the N42 source claims a sampler for the complete remaining photon-count vector conditioned on an exact herald. The claimed running time is polynomial in input bits, mode count, numerical herald count h, numerical mean energy E, and epsilon^-1, with no 1/p_H factor.
proof: The proposed sampler uses nonnegative relative branch counts for loop-hafnian coefficients, exact support/zero detection, rational denominator clearing, dummy padding, a simple-graph integer-weight gadget, and tail truncation. The complete N42 proof/code packet is absent from the supplied prior; only partial reconstruction and leaf audits are present.
cost: Charges rational bit growth, numerical h and E, graph size, inverse relative accuracy, confidence/log factors, finite random bits, and tail precision. It does not charge physical herald production. Dependence on OA113's worst-case polynomial-bit general-graph #PM service is essential.
baseline: Generic exact sequential loop-hafnian sampling is exponential in photon number. Full-law positive graph GBS sampling by Anand et al. does not sample arbitrary mixed/displaced heralds or fixed sectors. Rejection costs 1/p_H.
falsifier: A positive rational kernel violating the marginal closure or a disagreement in loop/singleton expansion, support detection, gadget count, tail bound, or confidence allocation invalidates the sampler composition.
sources: OA113 pinned primary release dated 23 Sep 2026: https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/A-Fully-Polynomial-Randomized-Approximation-Scheme-for-Perfect-Matchings-in-General-Graphs-September-23-2026/main.pdf
Mixed/displaced loop-hafnian formulas, Quesada et al. (2019): https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.07011
open_gate: Independent audit/replay of OA113's relative error, exact-zero, and worst-case bit-complexity theorem, followed by end-to-end N42 composition verification.
scope: N42 is source-reported; OA113 is a primary release claim not independently externally validated here. No novelty or priority claim.

claim: Integer-weighted edge to simple-unweighted perfect-matching gadget
theorem: For every positive integer W with k=ceil(log2(W+1)), a simple bipartite graph with O(k) vertices and O(k^2) edges has a two-port matching signature (1,W,0,0): one completion when neither port is used, W when both are used, and zero when exactly one is used.
proof: Build a DAG with vertices s,x_0,...,x_(k-1),t; add x_i->t and x_i->x_j for j<i; add s->x_i iff bit i of W is one. The number of x_i-to-t paths obeys P_i=1+sum_(j<i)P_j=2^i, so the s-to-t path count is W. Split each DAG vertex into L_v,R_v; add L_v-R_v and L_u-R_v for each arc u->v. The full graph has the unique all-loop perfect matching. Deleting ports L_t,R_s yields one completion per s-to-t path. Parity makes exactly-one-port use impossible.
cost: O(log W) vertices and O(log^2 W) simple edges. If weights are rational, clearing denominators charges their bit lengths.
baseline: A vague appeal to standard weighted matching gadgets would leave the weighted-to-unweighted reduction as a gap. This construction makes the elementary gadget explicit; it does not establish the OA113 FPRAS.
falsifier: A path-count error, unintended directed cycle, or port-signature mismatch disproves the gadget. Exact enumeration was performed for W=1,...,20 and matched the claimed signature.
sources: OA113 theorem page work/astra_prior/web/pages/d-f92e4f610d78fe0a.html for the separate unweighted counting service
open_gate: Independent end-to-end integration into N42, including zero singleton handling and error/confidence allocation.
scope: Proof is internally reconstructed; finite enumeration is a sanity check only.

claim: Exact coefficient-positivity criterion for centered gauge-invariant Gaussian states
theorem: For N>=0, Q=N(I+N)^(-1), and Bargmann density kernel det(I-Q) exp(z^T Q bar(w)), all coefficients in a fixed detector phase frame are real nonnegative iff every Q_ij is real nonnegative. Under local phase gauges, such a gauge exists iff all cycle phase products on the nonzero-entry graph equal one.
proof: Expand the exponential for sufficiency. The coefficient of z_i bar(w_j), divided by the constant coefficient, equals Q_ij, proving necessity. The cycle-product condition is the standard vertex rephasing consistency condition.
cost: Exact rational covariance inversion and phase-certificate acquisition are charged by the input representation; this is a representation test, not a sampler runtime theorem.
baseline: Positive covariance and positive P representation alone do not imply coefficient positivity. The thermal path matrix N=[[2,1,0],[1,2,1],[0,1,2]] has Q_13<0 after any eta>0 and a negative gauge-invariant triangle product, although unconditional counts have an easy Gaussian-Poisson sampler.
falsifier: A coefficient expansion with a negative coefficient despite all Q entries nonnegative, or a balanced-cycle graph with no nonnegative rephasing, would contradict the algebraic proof.
open_gate: Whether other positive representations efficiently sample frustrated-cycle or general mixed/displaced rare heralds remains UNKNOWN.
scope: Exact criterion within the centered gauge-invariant subclass, not a complexity boundary.

claim: A full variable-cardinality doubled-graph sampler does not automatically yield a fixed herald-sector sampler
theorem: For G consisting of m disjoint edges and c=1/2 in the graph-GBS law proportional to c^(2|S|) PM_G(S)^2, the feasible sector |S|=2 has exact mass (m/16)(16/17)^m. Thus rejection from the full law is exponential even though the sector is easy to sample directly.
proof: Feasible sets are unions of j edges, each with matching count one and weight 16^-j. The partition function is (17/16)^m, and the j=1 mass is the stated expression. In G square K2 the sector fixes a vertical-edge count; the full-law sampler controls perfectness, not this color count.
cost: Expected rejection count is (16/m)(17/16)^m. Direct conditional sampling is O(log m) random bits up to representation costs.
baseline: Anand et al. (2025/2026) give a polynomial-TV sampler for the complete variable-cardinality law; this exact example blocks a general inference by postselection/rejection.
falsifier: Direct binomial expansion or the exact doubled-graph identity would expose an arithmetic mistake. The calculation is exact.
open_gate: Direct colored-sector relative counting/sampling or certified coefficient extraction with polynomial conditioning.
scope: Counterexample to a generic reduction strategy only; no hardness claim.

claim: Conditional-TV amplification and sample-only rare-event lower bound
theorem: If two full flagged laws have TV delta and herald masses p,p'>0, their conditional laws obey TV<=3delta/[2 min(p,p')]; when p=p', TV<=delta/p. In the sample-only Bernoulli-herald black-box model, T unconditional samples that must identify an unknown postselected bit to error epsilon<1/2 satisfy T>=log(1/(2epsilon))/[-log(1-p)]=Omega(p^-1 log(1/epsilon)) for p<=1/2.
proof: Restrict the full-law L1 difference to the herald event, then account for normalization by the difference |p-p'|. For the lower bound couple the two black boxes on shared flags and coins; transcripts can differ only if at least one of T trials heralds.
cost: Physical rejection has mean 1/p and capped failure (1-p)^T. These lower bounds apply to black-box unconditional samples, not structured optical descriptions.
baseline: An N42-style relative branch-count algorithm can exploit a supplied optical description and avoid 1/p; N81's class implication only rules out polynomial log(1/p) dependence under its conditions.
falsifier: A pair of conditional distributions with equal herald masses violating delta/p, or a sample-only decision algorithm violating the coupling bound, would falsify the proof.
open_gate: None for the stated information-theoretic interface; structured-description complexity is a separate question.
scope: Proved for black-box samples; not a lower bound against all classical algorithms.

claim: Equal energy and herald probability do not determine the conditional optical law
theorem: A two-mode squeezed source and a product thermal source can be parameterized to have equal input energy and exactly equal herald probability under the same uniform loss, while conditioning on a herald count h=s^2 yields conditional outputs converging respectively to Poisson(1) and vacuum, with TV tending to 1-exp(-1). The common success probability is approximately s^(-6s^2).
proof: The leaf derives the exact geometric/thermal herald law and takes the s->infinity limit. The state pair has rational parameters of O(log s) bits while the numeric herald count is s^2.
cost: Physical rejection is superpolynomial; description-based samplers remain easy for both examples. Numeric herald count must be charged, so binary bit length alone hides a large output parameter.
baseline: Energy-only or success-probability-only covariance resets cannot control the conditioned output law.
falsifier: Exact normalization and the limiting probability laws are checkable from the two generating functions.
sources: Jerrum-Sinclair-Vigoda FPRAS source cited in the leaf
open_gate: No hardness claim; use as an adversarial control in any resource or conditioning theorem.
scope: Exact family-specific counterexample, not a sampler lower bound.

claim: Phase-twirled bipartite herald law admits a scoped positive latent sampler
theorem: Under the leaf's weighted phase-orthogonality and phase-independent-normalization assumptions for a bipartite centered pure Gaussian herald, the phase-twirled complete conditional count law, including collisions, can be sampled from a log-concave simplex latent law without inverse-herald rejection.
proof: Phase averaging removes cross monomials by weighted orthogonality; the surviving nonnegative sector weights define the simplex latent measure, whose normalized count draws generate the twirled conditional law.
cost: Exact theorem is algebraic; finite-bit sampling of the latent distribution and rational implementation costs remain unresolved. An l1-envelope rejection proposal has cost (5/4)^k on the leaf's k-copy fixture.
baseline: The leaf's result covers a phase-twirled ensemble, not a supplied fixed-phase instance. N81 blocks a uniform arbitrary-phase conditional sampler under its inherited collapse assumptions.
falsifier: A surviving cross-term under the stated orthogonality condition, or phase-dependent herald normalization, invalidates the factorization.
open_gate: Finite-bit sampler with certified TV and cost; general fixed-phase extension.
scope: Scoped ensemble theorem candidate; not externally reviewed.

claim: Spectrum-sensitive rank compression for unconditional lossy sampling
theorem: For passive channel singular values sigma_i and discarded-mode energy W_k=sum_(i>k) sigma_i^2 <n_(v_i)>, the leaf derives TV(P_T,P_Tk)<=sqrt(1-(1-W_k)_+^2), and composes it with N71 to control retained sixth-power spectral mass.
proof: The note bounds the discarded-mode vacuum overlap and converts it to trace/TV distance, then applies the inherited N71 reset sampler to the retained subspace.
cost: Nine one-mode loss fixtures and vacuum/thermal generating-function checks passed. Combined finite-bit sampler is unverified because the N73 high-precision engine was not executed.
baseline: N71/N73 unconditional reset sampling is the relevant comparator; neither is a specified rare-herald conditional sampler.
falsifier: A state/channel pair violating the discarded-mode vacuum-overlap inequality or any exact fixture mismatch.
open_gate: Independent proof review, finite-bit sampler execution, and extension to noncommuting channels.
scope: Candidate unconditional compression result; finite evidence only for fixtures.

claim: Universal all-mode inverse-polynomial-noise stability of rare-herald conditional laws is false
theorem: For R=4^k, lambda=2^(-R^2), fixed integer a>=1, nu=R^(-a), eta=1/R, a two-mode squeezed-vacuum source with rational Walsh-Hadamard fanout of the idler into R herald modes has ideal conditional signal law tending in TV to Poisson(1), while after uniform additive Gaussian noise on all R+1 modes before loss the conditional signal law tends in TV to vacuum. The conditional-law TV gap tends to 1-exp(-1).
proof: The ideal source pair number N is geometric. N<R cannot herald; the N=R branch has herald probability q_R=eta^R R!/R^R=R!/R^(2R). The conditional mass above R is at most lambda^2/[(1-lambda^2)q_R], which tends to zero, so the retained signal is Bin(R,1/R)+o_TV(1), hence Poisson(1). The TMSV pure-state trace distance from global vacuum is exactly lambda. Channel contractivity makes the full noisy output law lambda-close to the vacuum-plus-noise reference, which is product thermal with per-mode mean t=eta nu. Its all-one herald probability is p0=[t/(1+t)^2]^R. Since lambda/p0 tends to zero, the noisy conditional signal is o_TV(1) from the independent thermal law of mean t, which tends to vacuum.
cost: Rational input covariance has O(R^2) squeezing bits; fixed-a noise and loss have O(log R) bits; Walsh-Hadamard has R^2 rational dyadic entries and O(R^2 log R) bits. m=R+1, numeric h=R, 1/eta=R, input energy is O(R nu+lambda^2)<=O(R), noisy log inverse herald probability is Theta(R log R), and ideal log inverse herald probability is Theta(R^3). Retained conditional means tend respectively to 1 and 0.
baseline: A universal claim that inverse-polynomial noise preserves every rare-herald conditional law is false. This does not decide N81-specific noisy sampling complexity; both distributions in this witness are easy to sample.
falsifier: An error in the TMSV-vacuum trace distance, exact thermal reference herald mass, conditional-TV normalization, uniform fanout probability, or ideal tail bound invalidates the construction.
sources: Self-contained derivation in RESULT.txt, section 1, all-mode noise counterfamily
Gaussian optical event framework: Hamilton et al. (2016/2017), https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.01199
open_gate: Independent audit of the proof and exact rational optical interface; no hardness or sampler-complexity implication follows.
scope: Universal conditional-law stability is refuted at an internally derived candidate level. Does not automatically refute or prove robustness for N81 instances.

claim: Uniform inverse-polynomial noise creates an N81 herald-vacuum branch larger than its entire ideal herald
theorem: For N81's detector-plane uniform additive noise nu=R^(-a), eta=1/R, and herald with h ones and h0 zero targets, the input herald-vacuum block contributes at least p_floor=(1/2)t^h/(1+t)^(2h+h0), t=eta nu. The ideal pure herald mass obeys p_id<=(2g)^h(4/3)^(d/2). With N82's g=2^(-ell), ell>=(q+10)/2, q>=R ceil(log2R), and d,h,h0=O(R), p_floor/p_id diverges for every fixed a>0.
proof: The N81 mean energy E<=2dg^2 implies source probability of vacuum on all herald modes at least 1-E>=1/2. Phase-covariant additive noise, vacuum loss, and PNR detection give the exact-pattern probability t^h/(1+t)^(2h+h0) from this block. For the ideal pure source, G(x)=E[x^(N_total)]=sqrt(det(I-BB*)/det(I-x^2 BB*)); set x=1/(2g) so beta_j<=g implies G(x)<=(4/3)^(d/2). The event detects h photons and requires N_total>=h, hence p_id<=x^(-h)G(x). The exponent h log2(t/(2g)) dominates the O(R) determinant cost and the o(1) monitor penalty.
cost: Detector mode count d=O(R), numerical herald h=O(R), 1/eta=R, noise rational bits O(log R), and the existing N81 lower-bound bit size is O(R^2 log R).
baseline: This branch alone does not bound the full noisy conditional law; the conditioned positive-P posterior comparison is the stronger result in PC-03/PC-14.
falsifier: A failure of the vacuum-block herald probability, N81 energy/vacuum-mass bound, total-number generating function, or tail-Markov inequality invalidates the comparison.
open_gate: Independent audit of the branch estimate and PC-14 posterior comparison. Nonvacuum source branches are controlled by the full likelihood-ratio argument, not this floor alone.
scope: Shows a noise-generated herald branch larger than the entire ideal herald. The full N81 noisy conditional law is separately shown TV-o(1) from vacuum in PC-03/PC-14; no general hardness or sampler conclusion follows.

claim: Binary-herald posterior stability for weak centered Gaussians under dominant isotropic noise
theorem: Let a centered pure Gaussian on d modes have rational B with ||B||<=g<1/4. Add isotropic displacement noise nu>g/(1-g) to all modes and pure loss eta>0. For any binary PNR herald on H (h one-targets, h0 zero-targets, h<=|H|<=d), put t=eta nu and delta=g/[(1-g)nu]. If delta<=1/4 and d delta<=c, the complete unheralded count law conditioned on the herald is within O(sqrt(d delta)) TV of the same heralded law for the noise-only B=0 reference. The actual herald probability is p_ref exp(O(d delta)), p_ref=t^h/(1+t)^(2h+h0).
proof: The pure-state quadrature covariance obeys ||V_B-I/2||<=g/(1-g), so noise yields positive P covariance nu I+(V_B-I/2); after loss this is t(I+E), ||E||<=delta. Standardize reference latent quadratures to y~N(0,I). The reference posterior has independent radii with exact mgf E exp(theta||y||^2)=(1-2theta)^(-(d-|H|))(1-2theta/(1+t))^-(|H|+h). The Gaussian prior RN derivative r satisfies |log r(y)|<=C delta(2d+||y||^2), whence Z=E[r]=exp(O(d delta)), E[r^2]<=exp(O(d delta)), conditional chi-square<=exp(O(d delta))-1, and TV<=O(sqrt(d delta)). Photon counts are a common Poisson-mixture channel, so data processing preserves the bound.
cost: The bound depends on numerical dimension d and binary target count h through O(d delta); no inverse herald probability appears. For N81, d=O(R), g<=2^-R, nu=R^-a for fixed integer a>=1, so d delta=O(R^(a+1)2^-R).
baseline: Generic full-state trace continuity followed by conditioning incurs 1/p_ref and may fail. Posterior comparison works because each herald count is at most one, so the conditioned reference latent norm remains O(d).
falsifier: Check the exact coherent-quadrature convention, P covariance under additive noise and loss, gamma posterior law, and the likelihood-ratio second moment. The result as stated uses isotropic noise, a centered input, and binary herald targets.
open_gate: Independent proof review; extension to nonbinary herald counts, displacements, or nonisotropic noise requires a separate posterior-moment bound.
scope: Mathematical conditional-law candidate for weak centered Gaussian sources; not an efficient sampler theorem or complexity lower bound.

claim: Near-isotropic centered positive-P Gaussian optics admits a finite-bit approximate exact conditional PNR sampler without inverse-herald cost
theorem: Given rational t>0 and centered post-loss quadrature P covariance C=tA on d modes, a rational PSD certificate (1-eps_bar)I<=A<=(1+eps_bar)I with 0<=eps_bar<=1/4, and a PNR pattern k_j on s herald modes, the exact-real sampler based on N(0,ctI) conditioned on the same herald and rejection exp(-y^T[A^-1-c^-1I]y/2), c=1+eps_bar, samples the target conditional count law exactly. Its expected proposal trials are <=exp(C(d+kappa)eps_bar), independent of 1/p_H, where kappa=sum k_j is charged numerically. A dyadic finite-bit implementation has output-law TV <=eps_out+xi and worst-case time polynomial in rational input length L, d, numeric kappa, M_out=tT/2, eps_out^-1, log(xi^-1), and Lambda>=exp(C(d+kappa)eps_bar). A polynomial-in-L corollary additionally requires numeric kappa, M_out, eps_out^-1, and log(xi^-1) to be polynomially bounded in L; no such claim is made when the rational scale t makes M_out exponentially large in its bit length.
proof: The isotropic proposal posterior factorizes into independent uniform phases and Gamma radii: shape k_j+1, scale 2ct/(1+ct) on herald modes and shape 1, scale 2ct otherwise. In y=x/sqrt(t), f_A/f_c=M exp(-y^TDy/2), M=c^d/sqrt(det A), D=A^-1-c^-1I>=0. The determinant envelope cancels in conditional normalization; accepting with exp(-y^TDy/2) gives exactly the target P posterior. Under the proposal E||Y||^2<=2c(d+kappa), ||D||<=2eps_bar/(1-eps_bar^2), and Jensen implies alpha>=exp(-C(d+kappa)eps_bar). For finite bits, truncate the Gamma sum at T=4c[K log 2+log(8/rho)], K=d+kappa, couple dyadic uniforms/phases to Euclidean error O(rho/[1+sqrt(eps_bar)+sqrt(t)]), approximate acceptance and rational-rate Poisson kernels to O(rho), with rho=eps_out/(C Lambda); normalization costs at most Lambda and an O(Lambda log(1/xi)) attempt cap bounds timeout. Exact rational LDL/fraction-free arithmetic validates the certificate and computes D.
cost: Certificate validation, rational inverse, quadratic forms, interval arithmetic, and Poisson truncation are polynomial in d and exact matrix/noise/loss bit length L. Total numerical PNR count kappa is separately charged: the stated Gamma construction uses O(d+kappa) exponential variates and is not asserted polynomial in the binary length of an arbitrarily large herald number. The explicit output Poisson cutoff is Q=O(M_out+log(1/rho)), M_out=tT/2. No log(1/p_H) enters the algorithm. Physically generating and discarding failed optical trials still costs expected 1/p_H. Three rational diagonal two-mode fixtures exactly match the integrated acceptance and p_H/(M q_H) formulas; a 60-digit numerical check confirms Jensen on those fixtures only. A polynomial-in-L corollary also requires numeric kappa and M_out=tT/2, together with eps_out^-1 and log(xi^-1), polynomially bounded in L; rational t can make M_out exponential in its bit length. N81 satisfies these extra bounds.
baseline: Quesada–Arrazola arXiv:1908.08068 explicitly samples sequentially from Gaussian marginal probabilities by conditional ratios; by inference, a fixed-herald-prefix adaptation samples the remaining law without an inherent 1/p_H rejection factor, but costs O(m N^3 2^N) after N detected photons. Quesada et al. arXiv:1905.07011 compute heralded-state matrix elements and success probabilities via loop hafnians, with exponential mode/occupation costs. Positive-quasiprobability output samplers and Oh et al. arXiv:2306.03709 target full output distributions; the latter notes postselected state preparation only as a possible application. The exact-real proposal overhead is polynomial when (d+kappa)eps_bar=O(log L). A polynomial-bit runtime in L also requires numeric kappa, M_out, and the requested accuracy budgets to be polynomially bounded. This is not a claim that no direct conditional algorithm exists.
falsifier: An incorrect Gamma posterior or density ratio, failure of D>=0 under the certified interval, an acceptance probability below the Jensen bound, or a finite-bit coupling/count-kernel error exceeding the stated budget falsifies the result.
open_gate: Independent proof review of finite-bit coupling after conditional normalization; independent check of the inferred fixed-herald-prefix adaptation of the Quesada–Arrazola sequential sampler has the stated exp-in-photons cost and no hidden 1/p_H loss; and a primary-literature priority search. Extend beyond centered near-isotropic P covariances only with a separately proved posterior-moment and domination bound.
scope: Applies to centered rational positive-P Gaussian states with a supplied near-isotropy covariance certificate. claim: Gaussian exponential tilting and positive-count marginalization yield a conditional sampler with rejection cost controlled by total herald photons times tilted-marginal anisotropy
theorem: Let C be a rational strictly positive definite centered coherent-quadrature P covariance; let H be a PNR herald, H_+ its m positive-count modes, kappa the numerical total target count, and U the remaining modes. Put C°=(C^{-1}+P_H)^{-1}, S=C°_{H_+,H_+}, K=C°_{U,H_+}S^{-1}, V=C°_{U,U}-KSK^T. If (1-eps)bI<=S<=(1+eps)bI for rational b>0 and 0<=eps<=1/4, the exact conditional output-count law is sampled by q(x)=phi_{(1+eps)bI}(x)W(x)/( (1+eps)b)^kappa, acceptance exp[-x^T(S^{-1}-((1+eps)b)^{-1}I)x/2], then X_U|X_+=x~N(Kx,V) and independent Poisson counts of rates ||X_u||^2/2. Its expected proposal count is at most exp(2(1+eps)eps(m+kappa)/(1-eps^2))<=exp(6 kappa eps), independent of unheralded dimension, zero-target herald count, and 1/p_H. For kappa=0 the Gaussian tilt alone is exact.
proof: The herald likelihood factors as exp(-X^T P_H X/2)W(X_+). Gaussian completion of the square gives phi_C exp(-X^T P_H X/2)=z_H phi_{C°}; marginalization gives pi_+(x)=phi_S(x)W(x)/Z_S. Under the isotropic proposal, each positive herald radius has squared radius/2 distributed Gamma(k_j+1, scale cb), and Z_q=(cb)^kappa. With D=S^{-1}-(cb)^{-1}I>=0, the target/proposal ratio is a constant times exp(-x^TDx/2), so acceptance produces exactly pi_+ without computing Z_S or p_H. The certificate gives ||D||<=2eps/[b(1-eps^2)]; E_q||X||^2=2cb(m+kappa); Jensen yields the bound. Conditional Gaussian regression and Poisson mixing produce the requested law.
cost: Exact rational inverse/Schur/LDL preprocessing and certificate checks are polynomial in d and rational input bit length L. The Gamma proposal uses O(m+kappa) exponential variables, so numerical kappa is charged; this is not polynomial in the binary length of an arbitrary huge herald count. Physical optical repetition still costs 1/p_H. Under C=tA with (1-eps_bar)I<=A<=(1+eps_bar)I, the tilted positive-count block has eps_eff=eps_bar/[1+t(1-eps_bar)]<=eps_bar, giving proposal exponent O(kappa eps_eff).
baseline: Quesada-Arrazola arXiv:1908.08068 gives sequential Gaussian-boson conditional probability ratios with exponential dependence on detected photons; fixing the herald as a prefix is an inferred conditional adaptation. Quesada et al. arXiv:1905.07011 give loop-hafnian heralded-state matrix elements. Neither establishes this positive-P near-isotropic rejection bound.
falsifier: A sign or determinant error in the Gaussian tilt, a wrong Gamma shape/scale or factorial normalizer, failure of D>=0, or an accepted density other than phi_S W/Z_S invalidates the result. Exact-rational fixtures check correlated three-mode and all-zero cases but are not proof validation.
open_gate: Independent external proof review and novelty/priority search. The theorem is restricted to centered strictly positive-P inputs with a supplied rational near-isotropy certificate on S; displaced/non-positive-P and arbitrary anisotropic cases remain open.
scope: An exact-real abstract conditional sampler; not finite-bit implementation by itself, not physical herald production, not a hardness or complexity lower bound, and not a general mixed/displaced Gaussian boundary.

claim: The marginalized positive-P herald sampler admits a finite-bit approximate implementation with explicit rejection, Gaussian precision, output-rate, and photon-count costs
theorem: Under PC-16 and its supplied rational covariance certificate, for rational 0<delta,xi<1 there is a bounded-random-bit sampler with output-law TV<=delta+xi. Its worst-case bit and randomness cost is polynomial in d, rational input length L, numerical kappa, dyadic Lambda>=exp(6 kappa eps), explicit numeric M_out, delta^{-1}, log(xi^{-1}), and exact rational factorization/certificate bit lengths. A polynomial-in-L corollary requires numerical kappa, Lambda, M_out, delta^{-1}, and log(xi^{-1}) polynomially bounded in L. No p_H or log(1/p_H) factor occurs; physical optical repetition remains 1/p_H.
proof: Finite dyadic proposal, acceptance, and normal uniforms are coupled cellwise to exact uniforms. Proposal exponential sums have tail <=delta/(256Lambda); off this tail and the small-uniform event, the finite proposal is within Euclidean tau of the exact proposal. The acceptance function has Lipschitz constant sqrt(||D||/e), and a normalized rejection-coupling lemma loses at most O(Lambda) times the one-trial mismatch, yielding accepted-core coupling failure <=delta/16. The finite one-trial success probability is >=1/(2Lambda), so its uncapped expected proposal count is <=2Lambda (the exact-real expectation is <=Lambda). Exact rational LDL V=R diag(v)R^T and absolute dyadic square-root intervals give Lhat without relative precision for tiny pivots. The normal CDF is computed by integrating a bounded Taylor polynomial for exp(-x^2/2), with rational Machin intervals for pi; certified inverse-CDF bisection couples latent normals in Euclidean norm except for the explicit Gaussian-tail and endpoint bands. The product-Poisson Hellinger bound TV(Pois_x,Pois_y)<=||x-y||/sqrt(2) transfers amplitude coupling into count-law TV. A rational cap M_out bounds every finite sampled total rate; cutoff Q=O(M_out+log(1/delta)) and rational interval probabilities implement Poisson/multinomial draws. The deterministic rejection cap is O(Lambda log(1/xi)). No discrete-versus-continuous Gaussian TV assertion is used.
cost: See the full construction and constants in outputs/research/photonic_complexity/conditional_gaussian_finite_bit_theorem.txt. For kappa>0, K0=m+kappa, T=8(1+eps)b(K0+ceil(log2(256Lambda/delta))), B=ceil(sqrt(T)), r=2|U|, Rz=2ceil(log2(512r/delta)), and M_out=1/2[K_*ceil(sqrt(2m))B+(L_*+gamma_L)ceil(sqrt(r))(Rz+1)]^2. The Poisson cutoff is Q=ceil(16(M_out+ceil(log2(64/delta)))). For the all-zero herald, omit rejection and use the U marginal of C° with its analogous Gaussian output cap.
baseline: Direct Gaussian hafnian simulation and heralded-state loop-hafnian methods have exponential detected-photon/occupation costs in the cited formulations. PC-17 is a finite-bit implementation of PC-16 only on the positive-P near-isotropic certificate class; it does not dominate direct methods outside that interface.
falsifier: The proof fails if cellwise uniform coupling, the acceptance normalization lemma, the conditional LDL Gaussian coupling, the Poisson Hellinger normalization, or the finite Poisson tail/interval budget is invalid. In particular, a discretized Gaussian is not claimed TV-close to its continuous law.

claim: A modewise relative-covariance certificate extends conditional positive-P Gaussian herald sampling beyond one-scale near-isotropy
theorem: Let C be rational strictly positive definite, C°=(C^(-1)+P_H)^(-1), S=C°_(H_+,H_+), K=C°_(U,H_+)S^(-1), V=C°_(U,U)-KSK^T, with m=|H_+|>0 and numerical kappa=sum k_j. For rational D0=direct_sum_(j in H_+) b_j I2, b_j>0, and supplied exact PSD certificates 0<s_-D0<=S<=s_+D0, set rho=s_+/s_-, K0=m+kappa, and q=phi_(s_+D0)W/Z_q with Z_q=product_j(s_+b_j)^k_j. Accept q at x with probability exp[-x^T(S^(-1)-(s_+D0)^(-1))x/2]. This samples the exact conditional count law after Gaussian regression and Poisson mixing, with expected proposals <=exp[K0(rho-1)]. A dyadic bounded-bit implementation follows the PC-17 latent-coupling proof, with worst-case bit/randomness cost polynomial in d, rational input/certificate length, numerical kappa, Lambda=2^ceil(2K0(rho-1)), explicit numeric M_out, delta^(-1), log(xi^(-1)), and exact factorization bit lengths. Polynomiality in binary input length alone requires those numeric parameters to be polynomially bounded. No p_H or log(1/p_H) factor occurs in conditional sampling; physical herald generation still costs 1/p_H.
proof: Whiten with S′=D0^(-1/2) S D0^(-1/2). Its eigenvalues lie in [s_-,s_+], and D0^(1/2)[S^(-1)-(s_+D0)^(-1)]D0^(1/2)=S′^(-1)-s_+^(-1)I is PSD with operator norm at most 1/s_- -1/s_+. Under q, whitened mode radii are independent Gamma(k_j+1, scale s_+) and phases uniform, so E||D0^(-1/2)X||^2=2s_+K0. Jensen gives acceptance alpha>=exp[-K0(rho-1)]; the dyadic Lambda is an envelope since ln2>1/2. The finite-bit proof replaces the common scale in PC-17 by modewise scales; radial coupling uses b_max, the precision-gap Lipschitz bound uses the rational entrywise norm envelope, and the output Gaussian/Poisson smoothing is unchanged. The exact rational fixture checks a heterogeneous correlated two-mode core, its zero-tilt covariance reconstruction, normalizer, acceptance and energy bound.
cost: The full constants and finite-bit adaptation are in outputs/research/photonic_complexity/conditional_gaussian_modewise_preconditioner.txt. Set J=ceil(log2(256Lambda/delta)), T_Y=8s_+(K0+J), B_X=ceil(sqrt(b_max T_Y)), tau=delta/[512Lambda(1+Lbar_Delta+K_*)], and M_out=1/2[K_*ceil(sqrt(2m))B_X+(L_*+gamma_L)ceil(sqrt(r))(R_z+1)]^2. The attempt cap is O(Lambda log(1/xi)); Poisson inversion is polynomial in M_out. Covariance acquisition, exact rational sandwich checks, K,V, and LDL are charged. Numerical kappa,Lambda,M_out and delta^-1 are explicit; physical repeat-until-herald still costs 1/p_H.
baseline: PC-16/17 use a single scalar variance certificate. PC-18 permits arbitrary heterogeneity of the positive-herald mode scales when a rational relative Loewner sandwich controls standardized correlations. It still requires centered strictly positive-P input and a supplied certificate; it does not cover arbitrary anisotropic or displaced covariances, and no direct hafnian algorithm is dominated outside this certified class.
falsifier: A wrong modewise proposal normalizer, a sign error in the whitened precision gap, failure of the Gamma radial scale, an invalid Jensen bound, a missing b_max or dimension factor in the finite-bit coordinate coupling, or an uncharged M_out/accuracy cost would falsify the claim. claim: A local-matrix covariance certificate removes within-mode anisotropy from conditional Gaussian-herald rejection cost
theorem: Let C be a rational strictly positive definite centered coherent-quadrature P covariance, H an exact photon-number herald with counts k_j>=0, H_+ its positive-count modes, U the retained unheralded modes, m=|H_+|>0, and numerical kappa=sum_j k_j. Define C°=(C^(-1)+P_H)^(-1), S=C°_(H_+,H_+), K=C°_(U,H_+)S^(-1), V=C°_(U,U)-KSK^T. Let B=direct_sum_(j in H_+) B_j have rational SPD 2x2 blocks and suppose supplied exact rational PSD certificates 0<s_-B<=S<=s_+B. Put rho=s_+/s_-, K0=m+kappa, W(x)=product_j (||x_j||^2/2)^(k_j)/k_j!, and q(x)=phi_(s_+B)(x)W(x)/Z_q with Z_q=product_j s_+^(k_j) mu_(j,k_j), mu_(j,k)=E_(u uniform S1)(u^T B_j u)^k. The exact-real rejection sampler accepts q at x with probability exp[-x^T(S^(-1)-(s_+B)^(-1))x/2], then uses N(Kx,V) and independent Poisson intensities ||u_j||^2/2. It samples the complete conditional count record with expected proposals <=exp[K0(rho-1)]. For its bounded-bit implementation whiten y=B^(-1/2)x, set A=K B^(1/2), G=B^(1/2)(S^(-1)-(s_+B)^(-1))B^(1/2), and charge the output stage through a certified rational A_*>=||A|| rather than ||K||. With Lambda=2^ceil(2K0(rho-1)), the implementation has TV error <=delta+xi, finite uncapped mean proposals <=2Lambda, and attempt cap ceil(4Lambda ceil(log2(2/xi))). Its bit/randomness time is polynomial in d, rational input/certificate length L, numeric kappa, Lambda, numeric M_out=1/2[(A_*+gamma_A)Ymax+(L_*+gamma_L)c_r(Rz+1)]^2, delta^(-1), log(xi^(-1)), and exact rational/algebraic interval and factorization costs. Polynomiality in L alone requires numeric kappa,Lambda,M_out,delta^(-1) to be polynomially bounded. There is no p_H or log(1/p_H) in abstract conditional-record sampling; physical herald generation still costs 1/p_H.
proof: The proposal normalizer factors across modes. In an eigenbasis of B_j, with T=cos^2(theta)~Beta(1/2,1/2), expansion of (lambda_-+(lambda_+-lambda_-)T)^k gives the nonnegative mixture weights binom(k,l)lambda_-^(k-l)(lambda_+-lambda_-)^l binom(2l,l)/4^l and components Beta(l+1/2,1/2); the radial variable is Gamma(k_j+1,1). The angular moment mu_(j,k) is the exact rational even-cosine sum in the linked proof. Accepting q by the displayed precision-gap exponential gives density proportional to phi_S W. With Y=B^(-1/2)X, the transformed gap G is PSD and ||G||<=s_-^(-1)-s_+^(-1); E_q||Y||^2=2s_+K0, so Jensen gives alpha>=exp[-K0(rho-1)]. For finite bits the same proposal coupling is implemented in Y, with the explicit Gamma/Beta/normal-CDF schedules in the proof. A rational A_* is certified from algebraic intervals for A=K B^(1/2), the Gaussian output is factored by exact rational LDL and absolute-precision square roots, and latent Euclidean error is transferred to count TV by the product-Poisson Hellinger bound. This avoids any claim of TV closeness between a discrete Gaussian grid and a continuous Gaussian. The exact fixture verifies the covariance and output formulas for a constant-output, rare-herald, high-anisotropy family.
cost: See outputs/research/photonic_complexity/conditional_gaussian_local_anisotropic_sampler.txt, Sections 5-7. For J=ceil(log2(2048Lambda/delta)), T_Z=8(K0+J), Ymax=ceil sqrt(s_+T_Z), Lbar_a=1+1/s_-, and tau=delta/[512Lambda(1+Lbar_a+A_*)], the core is coupled in whitened coordinates to radius error tau with failure budget delta/(128Lambda). Beta-denominator, normal-tail, algebraic-eigenbasis, and categorical-mixture precision costs are explicit; mixture normalization uses mu_(j,k)>=(det B_j/tr B_j)^k and O(kL+log(k/epsilon_mix)) interval bits. Output uses exact rational LDL V=R diag(v) R^T, absolute precision for sqrt(v_i), inverse-normal Taylor/Machin intervals, and gamma_A,gamma_L,gamma_Z budgets. The finite Poisson cutoff is Q=ceil(16(M_out+ceil(log2(64/delta)))); numerical kappa,Lambda,M_out,delta^-1 and log(xi^-1) are charged. PC-19 does not pay 1/p_H abstractly; actual optical herald generation retains that cost.
baseline: PC-18 uses one scalar variance per herald mode; PC-19 uses a rational full 2x2 local block and removes its condition number from the rejection exponent, while still requiring a supplied useful standardized inter-mode sandwich. In the revised Section 8 family, local-matrix acceptance is one but every isotropic scalar proposal has acceptance <=sqrt(a)(1+a)/2=Theta(2^-n). This proves a weakness of that scalar proposal only: the two-mode k=1 family also admits a direct sampler using the same Gamma/Beta-mixture core law, a two-dimensional Gaussian, and one Poisson draw, and its generic low-herald-count hafnian baseline is easy. No general all-algorithm lower bound or quantum/classical separation follows.
falsifier: An incorrect angular mixture coefficient or Beta shape, failure of the rational angular normalizer, invalid supplied Loewner sandwich, loss of PSD for the precision gap, an omitted factor in the whitened finite coupling, an uncertified A_* or output-rate cap, a missing normal-CDF/small-denominator event, hidden numeric kappa/Lambda/M_out dependence, or an uncharged physical 1/p_H would falsify the corresponding claim.
